title: Introduce invocation-delta-writer and SLO primer for cross-tenant cost drift
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds a compact invocation delta writer to reduce telemetry volume and a SLO primer that surfaces cross-tenant cost drift signals. Backwards compatible.
description: Context: We observed noisy long-tail cost spikes across tenants where identical prompts produced divergent token costs due to mixed-model fallbacks and prompt rewriting. This PR introduces a compact invocation-delta-writer that emits incremental snapshot deltas for each invocation and a small SLO primer service that consumes deltas to produce per-tenant drift signals suitable for dashboards and alerting. Motivation: reduce telemetry cardinality, make cost drift actionable, enable early SLO guardrails. What this changes: 1) src/telemetry/delta_writer.py new streaming writer that deduplicates prefix KV and emits compact deltas keyed by invocation fingerprint. 2) src/telemetry/consumers/slo_primer.py lightweight service that aggregates deltas into drift indicators and exposes /metrics and /debug endpoints. 3) observability/dashboards/cost-drift-heatmap.json dashboard and panels for drift score, delta volume, and sample invocations. 4) infra/k8s/telemetry-deployment.yaml addition to deploy slo_primer as a low-CPU replica set with HPA. 5) tests/telemetry/test_delta_writer.py and integration tests that validate delta semantics and SLO thresholds. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] dashboard JSON - [x] infra manifests - [x] doc update in docs/observability/delta-writer.md Commits summary: 1) Add delta writer core loop and serializer 2) Add SLO primer aggregator and metrics endpoint 3) Add dashboard and example queries 4) Add tests and CI flakiness fixes 5) Update docs and runbook Changed files (high-level): src/telemetry/delta_writer.py new function DeltaWriter.write_delta(payload) which computes a fingerprint and emits minimal changed fields, src/telemetry/consumers/slo_primer.py new SLO aggregation loop, observability/dashboards/cost-drift-heatmap.json new panels, infra/k8s/telemetry-deployment.yaml, docs/observability/delta-writer.md, tests/telemetry/test_delta_writer.py, tests/integration/test_slo_primer.py, CI config tweaks in .github/workflows/telemetry.yml Review conversation snapshot: Reviewer Diego Martinez: "Nice approach to delta encoding, but worried about decoding cost on the metrics side. Can we keep a compact header to avoid full rehydration?" Author Aisha Khan: "Added a compact header (sha256 prefix + schema version) and lazy rehydration in slo_primer; updated tests to cover it." Reviewer Claire Nguyen: "SLO primer looks good. Please add rate limit and circuit breaker to protect downstream metrics store." Author reply: "Added token-bucket limiter and fail-open circuit with exponential backoff; documented behavior in runbook." Reviewer Sanjay Rao: "Can this be enabled incrementally by tenant?" Author: "Yes, delta_writer supports per-tenant sampling and slo_primer reads tenant enable flags from config service. Included Linear task ENG-1340 for rollout plan." CI summary: telemetry unit tests passed, integration suite passed in staging, flake fixed in second CI run, full matrix passed and benchmark job ran at reduced load. Performance notes: delta encoding reduced telemetry size by ~4.1x on a sample workload and slo_primer processes 10k deltas/s on a single vCPU with 50MB mem under bench harness. Rollout plan: start with 1% tenant sampling, increment to 10% after 48h, then cohort-based ramp tied to alert noise reduction. Merge: squash and merge to main, merge commit message includes short changelog and link to runbook. Backwards compatibility: telemetry consumer is optional; older consumers ignore delta header and process full snapshots; no breaking schema changes. Runbook and alerting: docs/observability/delta-writer.md contains suggested alerts: DriftScore > 0.15 for 30m => P1 review, DeltaVolumeDrop > 80% => investigate missing telemetry, RehydrationErrors > 0.5% => failover to snapshot stream. Notes and followups: ENG-1309 add tenant rollout dashboard, ENG-1340 phased rollout automation, SUP-4521 follow-up for a customer incident. Testing notes: added fuzzed payloads in tests to catch malformed deltas and verify graceful degradation. Links: Linear ENG-1309 ENG-1340, Jira SUP-4521, internal runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/delta-writer (internal).
